description: Solving partial differential equations numerically with the finite element method: boundary conditions, element meshes, eigenvalue problems, and the high-level PDE component functions for heat transfer, mass transport, solid mechanics, acoustics, electromagnetics and quantum mechanics.

tools.name: NDSolve
tools.description: Numerically solves ordinary and partial differential equations, returning solutions as InterpolatingFunction objects inside replacement rules. For PDEs on non-rectangular regions it uses the finite element method automatically when a region is given. It handles initial, boundary and mixed conditions.
tools.usage:
NDSolve[eqns, u, {x, y} \[Element] reg]
NDSolve[eqns, u, {t, 0, T}, {x, y} \[Element] reg]

parameters.name: AccuracyGoal
parameters.description: Target number of digits of accuracy.

tools.notes: NDSolveValue returns the solution function directly instead of a rule, which is usually more convenient.

tools.name: NDSolveValue
tools.description: Solves differential equations numerically and returns the requested solution function directly rather than a list of rules. It accepts the same equations, regions and options as NDSolve. Use it whenever you want to work with the solution immediately.
tools.usage:
NDSolveValue[eqns, u, {x, xmin, xmax}]
NDSolveValue[eqns, u, {x, y} \[Element] reg]

tools.name: DirichletCondition
tools.description: Specifies an essential boundary condition that fixes the value of the solution on part of the boundary. The second argument is a predicate selecting where the condition applies. It is the standard way to impose prescribed temperatures, displacements or potentials.
tools.notes: Where no condition is given, the natural (zero Neumann) condition applies by default.

tools.name: NeumannValue
tools.description: Specifies a natural boundary condition giving the flux across part of the boundary, added directly to the right-hand side of the PDE. It represents heat flux, surface load, current density or similar quantities. A predicate selects the boundary portion.
tools.notes: NeumannValue appears inside the equation, not as a separate condition, which is a common source of confusion.

tools.name: PeriodicBoundaryCondition
tools.description: Imposes periodicity between two parts of a boundary by mapping one onto the other with a transformation function. It is essential for unit-cell models of periodic structures. The predicate selects the target boundary and the transformation maps it to the source.

tools.name: ToElementMesh
tools.description: Creates a finite element mesh from a region, a set of boundary points or an existing mesh, with control over element order and size. It is in the NDSolve`FEM` context, loaded with Needs["NDSolve`FEM`"]. Use it when the automatic meshing inside NDSolve needs to be refined or inspected.

parameters.name: "MaxCellMeasure"
parameters.description: Upper bound on element area or volume.

tools.notes: Pass the mesh to NDSolve in place of the region to solve on exactly that discretization.

tools.name: ToBoundaryMesh
tools.description: Creates a boundary element mesh describing only the surface of a region, which can then be filled by ToElementMesh. It is useful when the boundary discretization must be controlled independently of the interior. It also lives in the NDSolve`FEM` context.

tools.name: ElementMesh
tools.description: Represents a finite element mesh, storing coordinates, element connectivity, element markers and boundary elements. Properties such as "Wireframe", "Quality" and "ElementMeshDirective" let you inspect and visualize it. It is the object that ToElementMesh returns.
tools.notes: Element markers let you assign different material properties to regions of the same mesh.

tools.name: ElementMeshInterpolation
tools.description: Builds an InterpolatingFunction from nodal values defined on an element mesh. It lets you evaluate and plot FEM results anywhere in the domain. Use it to post-process fields computed outside NDSolve.

tools.name: NDEigensystem
tools.description: Computes eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a differential operator on a region numerically, using the finite element method. Boundary conditions are given alongside the operator. Use it for vibration modes, waveguide modes and quantum bound states.
tools.usage:
NDEigensystem[op, u, {x, y} \[Element] reg, n]
NDEigensystem[{op, bcs}, u, vars, n]
tools.example:
{vals, funs} = NDEigensystem[
  {-Laplacian[u[x, y], {x, y}], DirichletCondition[u[x, y] == 0, True]},
  u, {x, y} \[Element] Disk[], 4];
vals
Plot3D[funs[[1]][x, y], {x, y} \[Element] Disk[]]
tools.notes: NDEigenvalues returns only the eigenvalues, which is faster when the modes are not needed.

tools.name: NDEigenvalues
tools.description: Computes only the numerical eigenvalues of a differential operator with given boundary conditions. It avoids the cost of assembling eigenfunctions. Use it for resonance frequencies and stability thresholds.
tools.example:
NDEigenvalues[{-Laplacian[u[x, y], {x, y}],
  DirichletCondition[u[x, y] == 0, True]}, u,
 {x, y} \[Element] Rectangle[{0, 0}, {1, 1}], 5]

tools.name: DEigensystem
tools.description: Computes symbolic eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a differential operator on simple regions. It returns exact closed forms when they exist. Use it for classical separable problems such as rectangles, disks and intervals.
tools.usage:
DEigensystem[op, u[x], {x, a, b}, n]
DEigensystem[{op, bcs}, u, vars \[Element] reg, n]
tools.example: DEigensystem[{-u''[x], DirichletCondition[u[x] == 0, True]}, u[x], {x, 0, Pi}, 3]
tools.notes: DEigenvalues gives only the eigenvalues symbolically.

tools.name: HeatTransferPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for heat conduction, convection and generation from a specification of material parameters. It removes the need to assemble the heat equation by hand and handles units. Use it together with HeatTransferValue boundary terms.
tools.usage: HeatTransferPDEComponent[{T[t, x, y], t, {x, y}}, pars]
tools.notes: Parameters may be given as Quantity objects with units, and the component then produces a dimensionally consistent equation.

tools.name: HeatTransferValue
tools.description: Generates boundary and source terms for heat transfer models, such as surface heat flux, convective cooling and radiation. It complements HeatTransferPDEComponent on the boundary. Use named parameter associations to describe the physical conditions.
tools.example:
HeatTransferValue[x == 1, T[t, x, y], t, {x, y},
  <|"SurfaceHeatFlux" -> 5|>]

tools.name: MassTransportPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for diffusion and convection of a chemical species, including reaction sources. It is the mass-transport counterpart of HeatTransferPDEComponent. Use it for concentration fields in flows and porous media.
tools.usage: MassTransportPDEComponent[{c[t, x, y], t, {x, y}}, pars]
tools.example:
pars = <|"DiffusionCoefficient" -> 0.01, "MassConvectionVelocity" -> {1, 0}|>;
MassTransportPDEComponent[{c[t, x, y], t, {x, y}}, pars]

tools.name: SolidMechanicsPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for linear and hyperelastic solid mechanics from material parameters such as Young's modulus and Poisson ratio. It produces the vector equilibrium equations for the displacement field. Use it for stress and deformation analysis.
tools.usage: SolidMechanicsPDEComponent[{{u[x, y], v[x, y]}, {x, y}}, pars]
tools.example:
pars = <|"YoungModulus" -> 200000, "PoissonRatio" -> 0.3|>;
SolidMechanicsPDEComponent[{{u[x, y], v[x, y]}, {x, y}}, pars]
tools.notes: SolidMechanicsStrain and SolidBoundaryLoadValue give post-processing and boundary-load terms.

tools.name: SolidMechanicsStrain
tools.description: Computes strain and stress quantities from a solid mechanics displacement solution. It returns the requested tensor components or derived measures such as von Mises stress. Use it to post-process structural results for plotting.
tools.example:
SolidMechanicsStrain[{{u[x, y], v[x, y]}, {x, y}},
  <|"YoungModulus" -> 200000, "PoissonRatio" -> 0.3|>, sol]

tools.name: SolidBoundaryLoadValue
tools.description: Generates boundary terms representing mechanical loads such as surface traction, pressure and fixed constraints. It is the boundary companion of SolidMechanicsPDEComponent. Loads are described with named parameter associations.
tools.example:
SolidBoundaryLoadValue[x == 1, {{u[x, y], v[x, y]}, {x, y}},
  <|"Pressure" -> 1000|>]

tools.name: AcousticPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for acoustic pressure waves, in time domain or frequency domain form. Parameters include sound speed, density and damping. Use it for room acoustics, ducts and transducer modelling.
tools.usage:
AcousticPDEComponent[{p[t, x, y], t, {x, y}}, pars]
AcousticPDEComponent[{p[x, y], {x, y}}, pars]
tools.example:
pars = <|"SoundSpeed" -> 343, "MassDensity" -> 1.2, "AngularFrequency" -> 2 Pi 500|>;
AcousticPDEComponent[{p[x, y], {x, y}}, pars]
tools.notes: AcousticRadiationValue, AcousticSoundHardValue and AcousticPressureCondition give the corresponding boundary conditions.

tools.name: AcousticRadiationValue
tools.description: Generates a non-reflecting radiation boundary condition for acoustic models, so that outgoing waves leave the domain without artificial reflection. It is essential for open-domain acoustic simulations. The predicate selects the outer boundary.
tools.example:
AcousticRadiationValue[x^2 + y^2 == 4, p[x, y], {x, y},
  <|"SoundSpeed" -> 343, "AngularFrequency" -> 2 Pi 500|>]

tools.name: ElectrostaticPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for electrostatics, relating electric potential to charge density through the permittivity. It handles anisotropic and spatially varying materials. Use it for capacitor design, field mapping and insulation studies.

tools.name: MagnetostaticPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for magnetostatic problems in terms of the magnetic vector or scalar potential. Permeability and current density are given as parameters. Use it for motor, transformer and magnet field computations.
tools.example:
MagnetostaticPDEComponent[{Az[x, y], {x, y}},
  <|"RelativePermeability" -> 1, "CurrentDensity" -> 1|>]

tools.name: SchrodingerPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for the time-dependent or stationary Schrodinger equation with a specified potential and mass. It lets quantum problems be posed directly in physical terms. Combine it with NDEigensystem to find bound states.

tools.name: FluidFlowPDEComponent
tools.description: Generates the PDE terms for incompressible fluid flow, covering Stokes and Navier-Stokes formulations. Parameters include density and dynamic viscosity. Use it for channel flows, cavity problems and low-Reynolds-number simulations.
tools.usage: FluidFlowPDEComponent[{{u[x, y], v[x, y], p[x, y]}, {x, y}}, pars]
tools.example:
FluidFlowPDEComponent[{{u[x, y], v[x, y], p[x, y]}, {x, y}},
  <|"MassDensity" -> 1, "DynamicViscosity" -> 0.01|>]

tools.name: LaplacianPDETerm
tools.description: Generates the Laplacian (diffusion) term of a PDE with an optional coefficient, in the sign convention used by the FEM solver. It is the lowest-level building block for assembling custom PDEs. Combine it with the other PDETerm functions.
tools.notes: Related terms: DiffusionPDETerm, ConvectionPDETerm, ReactionPDETerm, SourcePDETerm.

tools.name: DiffusionPDETerm
tools.description: Generates an anisotropic diffusion term with a scalar, vector or matrix diffusion coefficient. It generalizes LaplacianPDETerm to materials with direction-dependent properties. Use it for layered or fibrous media.
tools.example: DiffusionPDETerm[{u[x, y], {x, y}}, {{2, 0}, {0, 0.5}}]

tools.name: ConvectionPDETerm
tools.description: Generates a convection (advection) term with a given velocity field. Combined with diffusion it produces the convection-diffusion equation. Strongly convective problems may require stabilization options in NDSolve.
tools.example: ConvectionPDETerm[{u[x, y], {x, y}}, {1, 0}]

tools.name: ReactionPDETerm
tools.description: Generates a reaction (absorption) term proportional to the solution itself, with a specified rate coefficient. It models decay, absorption or linear source coupling. Combine it with diffusion and convection for full transport equations.
tools.example: ReactionPDETerm[{u[x, y], {x, y}}, 3]

tools.name: SourcePDETerm
tools.description: Generates a source term that does not depend on the solution, representing distributed forcing such as heat generation or body force. It is placed on the same side of the equation as the other PDE terms. Use it with the other PDETerm functions to build equations.
